IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Representatives Hunt, Appleton, Pollet, Roberts, and Santos

Bill.BriefDescription: Requiring DNA evidence prior to the imposition of the death penalty.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to requiring DNA evidence prior to the impositionof the death penalty; adding new sections to chapter 10.95 RCW;creating new sections; prescribing penalties; and providing aneffective date.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BillSection.RCWSLText: This act may be known and cited as the DNAtesting act of 2012.

(1) The legislature finds that: (a) Two hundred eighty people in the United States have beenexonerated from death row based on postconviction DNA testing; (b) On May 27, 2005, Texas passed a law stating that all felonsmust submit a DNA sample; (c) Gary Ridgway, the Green River Killer, was identified as beingguilty based on DNA evidence; (d) In Maryland on January 1, 2004, a student senate passed a billmandating postconviction DNA tests prior to the implementation of thedeath penalty; and p. 1 HB 2754 (e) A similar proposal was submitted to the Washington statelegislature in 2007 as House Bill No. 1890. (2) The purposes of this act are: (a) To prevent the incarceration or wrongful execution of innocentpersons; and (b) To alleviate the financial burden placed on taxpayers duringthe appeals process of a death sentence for individuals who may beexonerated later.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 10.95 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: (1) Except as provided in subsection (2) of this section, the stateof Washington may not impose the death penalty upon any personconvicted of aggravated first degree murder unless DNA evidence isintroduced and assists in the person's conviction. (2) The death penalty may be implemented without DNA evidence if: (a) The defendant has confessed to committing aggravated firstdegree murder; or (b) There is technological evidence that shows that the defendantcommitted aggravated first degree murder.

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 10.95 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: The definitions in this section apply to sections 1 through 3 ofthis act unless the context clearly requires otherwise. (1) "Accused" means a person against whom a criminal action isbrought. (2) "Aggravated first degree murder" has the same meaning as in RCW10.95.020. (3) "Confession" means a written or oral acknowledgment of guilt bya person accused of an offense. (4) "Crime" means a serious violation of public law. (5) "Exonerated" means the freeing or clearing from accusation orguilt. (6) "Implement" means to enforce or fulfill a duty. (7) "Postconviction DNA testing" means DNA testing that convictedpersons may request after their conviction. HB 2754 p. 2 (8) "Show" means to make manifest or apparent or to demonstrate,display evidence, or reveal. (9) "Technological evidence" means advanced or sophisticateddevices that furnish proof, including video cameras.

(1) This act applies to all state law, andthe implementation of that law, whether statutory or otherwise, andwhether adopted before, on, or after the effective date of thissection. (2) Statutory law adopted on or after the effective date of thissection is subject to the requirements of this act unless the lawexplicitly excludes such application by reference to this act.
Nothing in this act shall be construed toaffect, interpret, or in any way change the Constitution of the UnitedStates or the Constitution of the state of Washington.
